blocks.caption: Label Lab is designed as a focused production tool rather than a general-purpose 3D editor.

spans.text: Packaging artwork often looks finished in two dimensions but still needs a believable product presentation. Label Lab brings that gap into one controlled desktop workflow: choose a package, apply the artwork, tune the material and lighting, then export the result.
A design team may need to preview the same label across several cans, bottles and trays. Rebuilding every scene manually slows down comparison and makes output inconsistent.
The application turns recurring 3D setup into reusable product presets while keeping the creative controls needed for artwork placement, materials, environments and camera output.

The interface organizes the workflow around real packaging decisions. Product categories and packing sizes load as reusable data, imported artwork can be cropped and positioned on the selected surface, and visual settings remain close to the object being edited.

spans.text: Browse structured bottle, can, tray and podium variants without rebuilding the scene.
Import, crop, zoom and offset label artwork while retaining the state of each customizable part.
Adjust materials, colors, HDRI environments, lighting and product framing before export.

blocks.text: A controlled visual pipeline inside Unity

spans.text: Label Lab uses Unity 6 and HDRP as the rendering foundation. Product and environment resources are loaded through Addressables, while dedicated capture tools handle standard screenshots, tiled high-resolution output, transparent composition and video recording.
The result is a reusable studio where presentation quality comes from repeatable controls instead of a one-off scene setup.

blocks.alt: Label Lab application icon made from stacked geometric planes

spans.text: The application is packaged as a Windows x64 product with versioned releases, signed update manifests and downloadable builds delivered through Cloudflare R2. The current audited build is Label Lab 1.1.5, produced from a repeatable release pipeline rather than an editor-only prototype.
